holidays.name: National Noodle Day
holidays.description: A day for slurping, twirling and swirling every kind of noodle, from spaghetti and ramen to pad thai and lo mein. It's a good excuse to eat a big bowl of carbs without feeling guilty.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly favorite for pasta lovers, noodle shops and home cooks.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known noodles were found at the Lajia archaeological site in northern China. They are about 4,000 years old and were made from millet.

holidays.name: Change a Light Day
holidays.description: A bright idea of a holiday that asks you to swap an old, power-hungry bulb for an energy-efficient one. It's a small chore that can lower your electric bill and shrink your carbon footprint.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is usually tied to energy-saving campaigns and is often placed near the start of fall, when the days get shorter and people use more indoor lighting.
holidays.funFact: LED bulbs use far less energy than old incandescent bulbs and can last for many years. That means one swap can save you a lot of ladder trips.

holidays.name: National Badger Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the badger, a stocky, stripe-faced digger with a famously feisty attitude. Fans celebrate with wildlife facts, nature walks and a lot of admiration for an animal that doesn't back down.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It gives nature fans a reason to spotlight a often-misunderstood woodland animal.
holidays.funFact: A group of badgers is called a cete. Badgers dig large underground burrow systems called setts, and some of these have been used for generations.
